title: Je veux dire…
subtitle: Four ways to explain yourself
review: Written by Claude. Check the French, the English lines, the notes and the questions.
intro: A suspicious cake, a shrunken jumper, a plant that is 'resting' and a sofa with a spring sticking out: four short scenes between Emma and Lucas. Listen for the little phrases they use to correct themselves, explain again and play for time.

lines.text: Alors, il est comment, mon gâteau ?
lines.note: Il est comment ? Spoken word order: the question word goes at the end.

lines.text: Il est… spécial. Enfin, je veux dire, original.

tr.en: It's… unusual. Well, I mean, original.

lines.note: Spécial is faint praise: closer to 'odd' than to 'special'. Enfin, je veux dire: he backtracks.
Ou plutôt swaps in a more exact word.

lines.text: Si, si ! En fait, il est à quoi ?

tr.en: I do, I do! Actually, what flavour is it?

lines.note: Si says yes to a negative: Tu n'aimes pas. — Si ! Il est à quoi ? asks the flavour of a cake or an ice cream.

tr.en: Emma, I did a load of washing.

lines.note: Faire une lessive: to do a wash.

lines.text: Ton pull bleu a… un peu changé.

tr.en: Your blue jumper has… changed a bit.

lines.note: As a question, c'est-à-dire ? asks the other person to explain.
C'est-à-dire que + a full sentence gives the explanation.

lines.text: Autrement dit, tu l'as fait rétrécir.

tr.en: In other words, you shrank it.

lines.note: Faire rétrécir: to make something shrink.

lines.text: Ce que je veux dire, c'est qu'il ira très bien au chat.

tr.en: What I mean is, it will fit the cat perfectly.

lines.note: Aller à quelqu'un: to fit or suit someone. Ça te va bien: it suits you.

lines.text: Je suis rentrée ! Elle va bien, ma plante ?

tr.en: I'm home! Is my plant all right?

lines.note: Rentrée is feminine, because Emma is speaking.

tr.en: Well… how can I put it…
Let's say I thought about it.

lines.note: Penser à becomes y: j'y ai pensé.

lines.text: Je sais pas comment dire… Elle se repose.

tr.en: I don't know how to put it… It's resting.
We need to replace this sofa.

lines.note: Après here is not 'afterwards': it adds a 'but'.

lines.text: Y a un ressort qui dépasse ! Non mais je veux dire, on peut plus s'asseoir.

tr.en: There's a spring sticking out! No, but I mean, you can't sit on it any more.

lines.note: Y a = il y a. On peut plus = on ne peut plus: 'no longer', not 'more'.

lines.text: Cela dit, il a du caractère.
Tu vois ce que je veux dire, ou pas ?

tr.en: Do you see what I mean, or not?

lines.text: Je vois surtout le prix d'un canapé neuf.

tr.en: What I mostly see is the price of a new sofa.

notes: Je veux dire and enfin correct what you just said. Ou plutôt swaps in a better word. En fait gives the real version.
C'est-à-dire ? asks for an explanation; c'est-à-dire que… gives one. Autrement dit draws the conclusion.
Comment dire…, disons que… and en quelque sorte buy time, or soften bad news.
Genre, après and cela dit are spoken qualifiers: 'like', 'mind you', 'that said'.
Si says yes to a negative: Tu n'aimes pas. — Si !
Spoken French drops ne and shortens il y a: je sais pas, on peut plus, y a.

questions.q: Lucas calls the cake « spécial », then backtracks. Which phrase does he use to correct himself?
questions.why: Enfin, je veux dire… = 'well, I mean…': the usual way to take a word back.

questions.q: Emma wants Lucas to explain what « un peu changé » means. What does she ask?
questions.why: C'est-à-dire ? = 'meaning?'. It asks the other person to spell it out.

questions.q: Emma asks if her plant is dead. Lucas gives a cautious yes. What does he say?
questions.why: En quelque sorte = 'in a way', 'sort of'.

questions.q: Lucas admits the sofa is old, then adds a point in its favour. Which word opens his objection?
questions.why: Après, il est confortable = 'mind you, it's comfortable'.
